title: Plan by year, with windows and spread costs

blocks.text: Finance read the first plan and sent it back:

Your plan spends $13.14M in 2027. We have $8.89M that year. The $38.39M was five yearly budgets added up, and they are not interchangeable: money not spent in a year does not roll over. Plan by year. A project may start in any year of its window, and its cost lands in the years it is worked on, not all at the start. And no plan may run past 2031.

You start from the one-envelope planner of the lesson before. Change it to plan by year. Read each project's cost profile and latest start and each year's budget from the export, and let the model choose the year each funded project starts, inside its window. A project's cost is spent over its years of work, and each year's spend stays within that year's budget. No project may be funded with work that runs past the plan's last year. The plan says the year each funded project starts, and the report shows each year's spend against its budget.

`Request.starts` is a stub in `cipt/data.py` that returns the earliest year alone; `Project` needs the arithmetic of its profile too: how many years its work lasts, and what it spends in each calendar year for a given start. The report keeps its status line and its project lines and changes in two ways, every amount in whole $k with thousands commas:

items: the funded line's budget is the total of all yearly budgets: `funded <n> of <all> projects, capex $<capex>k of $<sum of yearly budgets>k, value $<value>k`, where value is still the funded projects' earliest-start value;
after it, before the project lines, one line per plan year in year order: `  <year>  spend $<spend>k of $<budget>k` (two spaces before the year and two after it), with 0 for a year nothing spends in.

blocks.text: Run executes `main.py`, which plans the demo export and prints the report; `expected/report.txt` is the report it should print. Submit runs every test in `tests/`, the earlier steps' included, and compares Run's report with the expected one.
Write each method below. The tests check each one by itself and the whole program end to end, so you may change any other part of the code as you see fit.

items: **Contract.** Takes a Request. Returns a Built with one binary x[(id, t)] per project and allowed start year t, a row `once_<id>` per project (it starts at most once), a row `budget_<y>` per plan year (that year's spread spend within that year's budget), and the summed value of the starts as the objective to maximize.
**Modeling idea.** A start-year variable per project and year carries the when, and the window is the set of variables that exist: a start outside it has no variable at all.

**Taught in** [6.4.1 Start-Time Variables x[i,t] and Timing Windows](../../../../06-formulation-craft/26-multi-period-timing/units/unit-01/6.4.1-start-time-variables-x-i-t-and-timing-windows.unit.html).

**Contract.** Returns the start years a project may use: from the later of its earliest start and the plan's first year, to the earlier of its latest start and the last year that lets all its work end inside the plan. An empty range when no start fits.
**Modeling idea.** Cutting the window in the data keeps the model free of rows that only forbid impossible starts.

**Taught in** [6.4.1 Start-Time Variables x[i,t] and Timing Windows](../../../../06-formulation-craft/26-multi-period-timing/units/unit-01/6.4.1-start-time-variables-x-i-t-and-timing-windows.unit.html).

blocks.text: def spend_by_year(request: Request, x: dict) -> dict[int, mathopt.LinearSum]

items: **Contract.** Returns one linear expression per plan year, with an entry for every plan year (an empty sum when no start can spend in it): for every project and allowed start, each year's amount of its cost profile times that start's variable, summed into the calendar year it is spent in.
**Modeling idea.** A start in year t spends profile[k] in year t + k, so a yearly budget row sums over starts, not over projects.
**Taught in** [6.4.2 Cash-Flow Spreading Across Years](../../../../06-formulation-craft/26-multi-period-timing/units/unit-02/6.4.2-cash-flow-spreading-across-years.unit.html).

blocks.text: def read_plan(built: Built, result: mathopt.SolveResult) -> Plan

items: **Contract.** Turns a SolveResult into a Plan whose starts map each funded project to the year its variable is 1.
**Modeling idea.** The schedule is read off the variables that are 1; the key of each variable says the year.

**Taught in** [6.4.1 Start-Time Variables x[i,t] and Timing Windows](../../../../06-formulation-craft/26-multi-period-timing/units/unit-01/6.4.1-start-time-variables-x-i-t-and-timing-windows.unit.html).

blocks.text: def spend_by_year(request: Request, plan: Plan) -> dict[int, int]

items: **Contract.** Returns what a Plan spends in each plan year, in whole $k, from the funded projects' starts and cost profiles, with 0 for a year nothing spends in.
**Modeling idea.** Compute the report's numbers from the plan and the data, not from the model, so the report checks the model instead of repeating it.

**Taught in** [14.2.2 Many Years: Start Years, Windows and Cash-Flow Spreading](../../../../14-growing-real-projects/55-project-cipt-planner/units/unit-02/14.2.2-many-years-start-years-windows-and-cash-flow-spreading.unit.html).

blocks.text: def render(request: Request, plan: Plan) -> str

items: **Contract.** Returns the report: the status line, the funded line with the total of all yearly budgets, one line per plan year reading `  <year>  spend $<spend>k of $<budget>k`, then one line per funded project.
**Modeling idea.** A yearly budget is only trusted when the report shows each year against its own limit.

**Taught in** [14.2.2 Many Years: Start Years, Windows and Cash-Flow Spreading](../../../../14-growing-real-projects/55-project-cipt-planner/units/unit-02/14.2.2-many-years-start-years-windows-and-cash-flow-spreading.unit.html).

**Contract.** Builds a Request from the export's dictionary: each project's cost profile, NPV for its earliest start, earliest and latest start; the plan's years; and the budget of each year, keyed by an int year. Refuses duplicate project ids.
**Modeling idea.** Read the columns the model needs now, and only those.

**Taught in** [14.2.2 Many Years: Start Years, Windows and Cash-Flow Spreading](../../../../14-growing-real-projects/55-project-cipt-planner/units/unit-02/14.2.2-many-years-start-years-windows-and-cash-flow-spreading.unit.html).

"""CIPT planner: which capital projects to fund, grown one planner request at a time.

The data it ships with (data/demo.json) is GridCap, a fictional utility invented for this course.
"""

"""python -m cipt EXPORT.json: plan the export and print the report."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

from .data import read_request
from .report import render
from .solve import solve


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="cipt", description="Plan a capital portfolio.")
    parser.add_argument("export", help="the planning export, a JSON file")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    request = read_request(args.export)
    print(render(request, solve(request)))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Solve a request with HiGHS and read the answer back as a Plan."""

from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes
import os
import sys

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt
from ortools.math_opt.solvers import highs_pb2

from .data import Request
from .model import Built, build
from .plan import Plan

#: One thread, set in HiGHS's own options; the first HiGHS solve of a process fixes the count.
PARAMS = mathopt.SolveParameters(highs=highs_pb2.HighsOptionsProto(int_options={"threads": 1}))


def run_highs(model: mathopt.Model) -> mathopt.SolveResult:
    """Solve with stdout pointed at /dev/null, so HiGHS's stray C output stays out of reports."""
    sys.stdout.flush()
    saved, sink = os.dup(1), os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY)
    os.dup2(sink, 1)
    try:
        return mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS, params=PARAMS)
    finally:
        ctypes.CDLL(None).fflush(None)
        os.dup2(saved, 1)
        os.close(saved)
        os.close(sink)


def read_plan(built: Built, result: mathopt.SolveResult) -> Plan:
    """Turn a solver result into a Plan: each funded project with the year its x is 1."""
    status = result.termination.reason.name.lower()
    if not result.has_primal_feasible_solution():
        return Plan(status=status)
    values = result.variable_values()
    starts = {pid: t for (pid, t), var in built.x.items() if values[var] > 0.5}
    return Plan(status=status, starts=starts, objective=result.objective_value())


def solve(request: Request) -> Plan:
    built = build(request)
    return read_plan(built, run_highs(built.model))

"""Run: plan the demo export and print the planners' report.

data/demo.json is GridCap tiny, a fictional utility's portfolio. Its path is taken from this
file's folder, never from the working directory, so the report is the same wherever Run starts.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from cipt.__main__ import main

DEMO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "data" / "demo.json"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main([str(DEMO)]))

"""The plan as the planners read it."""

from __future__ import annotations

from .data import Request
from .plan import Plan


def render(request: Request, plan: Plan) -> str:
    lines = [f"{request.name}: {plan.status}"]
    funded = [request.project(pid) for pid in plan.funded]
    capex = sum(p.capex for p in funded)
    value = sum(p.value for p in funded)
    lines.append(f"funded {len(funded)} of {len(request.projects)} projects, "
                 f"capex ${capex:,}k of ${request.capital_budget:,}k, value ${value:,}k")
    for p in funded:
        lines.append(f"  {p.project_id}  start {plan.starts[p.project_id]}  "
                     f"capex {p.capex:>6,}  value {p.value:>6,}  {p.name}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def spend_by_year(request: Request, plan: Plan) -> dict[int, int]:
    """Returns what a Plan spends in each plan year, in whole $k, from the funded projects' starts and cost profiles, with 0 for a year nothing spends in."""

"""Solve a request with HiGHS and read the answer back as a Plan."""

from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes
import os
import sys

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt
from ortools.math_opt.solvers import highs_pb2

from .data import Request
from .model import Built, build
from .plan import Plan

#: One thread, set in HiGHS's own options; the first HiGHS solve of a process fixes the count.
PARAMS = mathopt.SolveParameters(highs=highs_pb2.HighsOptionsProto(int_options={"threads": 1}))


def run_highs(model: mathopt.Model) -> mathopt.SolveResult:
    """Solve with stdout pointed at /dev/null, so HiGHS's stray C output stays out of reports."""
    sys.stdout.flush()
    saved, sink = os.dup(1), os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY)
    os.dup2(sink, 1)
    try:
        return mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS, params=PARAMS)
    finally:
        ctypes.CDLL(None).fflush(None)
        os.dup2(saved, 1)
        os.close(saved)
        os.close(sink)


def read_plan(built: Built, result: mathopt.SolveResult) -> Plan:
    """Turn a solver result into a Plan; a funded project starts in its earliest year."""
    status = result.termination.reason.name.lower()
    if not result.has_primal_feasible_solution():
        return Plan(status=status)
    values = result.variable_values()
    starts = {pid: built.request.project(pid).earliest_start
              for pid, var in built.x.items() if values[var] > 0.5}
    return Plan(status=status, starts=starts, objective=result.objective_value())


def solve(request: Request) -> Plan:
    built = build(request)
    return read_plan(built, run_highs(built.model))
